title: 3 Snubbed Post-Selloff Buys for 7%+ Dividends and Double-Digit Upside
text:
Shutterstock photo By Michael Foster
Wondering if itaEURtms too late to cash in on the late-2018 market mayhem?
If so, great news! There are still plenty of bargains to be had. And today IaEURtmm going to show you three great funds that are still cheap (though they wonaEURtmt be for long).
The best part? Each throws off hefty dividends upwards of 7%!
Of course, when discounts like the ones on these three exist, youaEURtmre right to ask why. The answer is simple: because these three funds are closed-end funds (CEFs) , theyaEURtmre off most peopleaEURtms radar. That means theyaEURtmre slower to snap back from a market decline than, say, a fan favorite like Apple ( AAPL ). So we still have time to tap them for serious upside.
More on these three buys in a moment.
First, letaEURtms look at why the buying opportunity in stocks (and funds) is far from overaEUR"and why the bull still has plenty of room to run.
The One Thing Nobody Tells You About Selloffs
HereaEURtms something you never hear after a market meltdown: these wipeouts reset future expectations for growthaEUR"and that makes it easier for companies to surprise investors when they next repor t earnings .
This is exactly where we are now.
HereaEURtms what I mean: according to FactSet, analysts have lowered their expectations for first-quarter 2019 earnings by 5%, the largest drop since 2015. And it just so happens that 2015 was the worst post-crisis year for stocks, with a late-year crash that looked a lot like what we saw starting in October 2018:
2015 Is Back!
Investors who ignored this noise and doubled down saw a 10% annualized return if they bought after 2015aEURtms earnings forecasts flopped. Why? Because 2015aEURtms lowered estimates led to a big upside surprise when profits skyrocketed over the longer term:
Earnings Soar Despite Pessimism
Anyone who bought in late 2015 or early 2016 caught the market when its P/E ratio was temporarily depressed. WeaEURtmre in the same situation now.
Not all market downturns are buying opportunities, though. For instance, it was a great time to sit things out when stocks dipped in early 2007. ThataEURtms because the housing bubble artificially buoyed confidence, so the market took months to price in the massive decline in earnings that was underway:
Crash Warning (in Orange) Is Ignored
Now compare that chart to 2018, keeping in mind that fourth-quarter data isnaEURtmt out yet:
No Warning Sign Here!
What these charts tell us is clear: 2018 is more like 2015 than 2007, where thereaEURtms a panic and strong growth instead of 2007aEURtms market euphoria and sudden collapse in growth. ThataEURtms a buying, not a selling, opportunity, especially as stocks still havenaEURtmt gotten back to their pre-October levels.
3 CEFs Poised for Post-Rebound Gains (and Yielding 7%+)
This is where the three funds I have for you today come in. The best thing about them is that each gives you a big part of your rebound profits in cash, thanks to their massive 7%+ dividends.
LetaEURtms start with my first pick, the Nuveen NASDAQ 100 Dynamic Overwrite Fund ( QQQX ), payer of a stable 7.8% dividend. It remains 22.6% off its price high, but more crucially, its massive premium to net asset value ( NAV ) has evaporated, letting you buy at a fair price for the first time in nearly a year:
QQQX Goes on Sale
Next up, the Liberty All-Star Growth Fund ( ASG ) pays an 8.2% dividend and holds many small- and mid-cap holdings. ItaEURtms also cheap, with a 7.8% discount to NAV thataEURtms near its lowest point in almost two years. That discount and ASGaEURtms focus on smaller firms were the cause of some volatility in late 2018, but a rebounding market makes this fund a huge opportunity now:
ASGaEURtms Ride Up Is Just Getting Started
This fundaEURtms 10.9% price return in 2019 is one of the best of any CEF, and thanks to lowered expectations, thereaEURtms still plenty of room for more gains.
LetaEURtms wrap up with the Eagle Capital Growth Fund ( GRF ). With large-cap holdings like PepsiCo (PEP) and Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A), this is a CEF that focuses on steadier stocks while still delivering upside. Its 7.3% dividend yield is nothing to sneeze at, either.
WhataEURtms more, the market seems to have forgotten GRFaEURtms 8.1% price decline in 2018, because itaEURtms still down 1.4% so far in 2019. Plus its discount remains near a five-year low:
This Buying Opportunity IsnaEURtmt Over
This is a rare gem of a fund with a big dividend and a strong portfolio that hasnaEURtmt caught much attention lately. That sets it up for some nice price gains in a continued recovery.
